I would keep my land in the winter wheat and summer maize double-cropping system. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this rotation fits my climate, my machinery, and my water constraints better than experimenting with lower-certainty cash crops. At 65, I would choose a system that is reliable, well understood, and easy to manage on time. Because I am well educated, I would lean on improved or hybrid seed, soil testing logic, and tighter input control instead of farming by habit alone. For winter wheat, I would focus on stable population, moderate fertilizer, two to three irrigations depending on rainfall, and tighter disease monitoring in spring. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize to preserve soil moisture and heat units, using hybrid seed, one-shot basal fertilizer plus a topdress if needed, and fewer irrigations unless summer rain fails. I would avoid excessive nitrogen because it wastes money, raises lodging risk, and reduces input efficiency. I would use rotary tillage after harvest where needed for residue handling, but keep operations simple and mechanized. My goal would be steady yield, manageable labor, and lower production risk rather than chasing the absolute maximum output.
